task: I need a periodic backup system that I can manage from the admin panel settings. I want it to automatically send me a copy of the database at set intervals. I also need a backup restore and export section, and it needs to be very flexible and robust—a cohesive system designed correctly, in line with the code, and following best practices.

findings.title: HTML tag mismatch: closed by in restore confirmation prompt
findings.detail: cb_backup_restore_prompt opens but closes on the same line. With parse_mode=html (set by safe_edit), Telegram cannot match the bold closing tag, so the backup id renders un-bolded or the message may error. The sibling delete-confirm handler at line 268 correctly uses . The router test test_cb_backup_restore_prompt_uses_service only asserts '#1' in text and never validates tag balance.

findings.title: _safety_backup copies a WAL-mode DB without checkpointing
findings.detail: The Database runs in WAL mode (database.py:31 sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL). _safety_backup copies only bot.db via shutil.copy2 without checkpointing the WAL. Committed transactions residing only in the WAL are absent from the safety copy, so a rollback during a failed restore could write an incomplete DB. The module docstring (line 19) claims 'the live DB is checkpointed' but no checkpoint occurs in this path.

findings.title: Safety backup files (safety-*.db/safety-*.key) never cleaned up after restore
findings.detail: _safety_backup writes safety-{stamp}.db and safety-{stamp}.key into backups/. The _swap finally block (line 496) only rmtrees the _stage/ directory; the safety files persist on every restore, leaking two files per run. Over time, repeated restores accumulate orphaned safety files.

findings.title: Stale WAL/SHM files remain after _install overwrites bot.db
findings.detail: _install copies the backup bot.db over the live file but leaves the old -wal/-shm files. SQLite's WAL salt mismatch should cause it to ignore them, but this is not guaranteed across all SQLite versions and is fragile. Best practice is to explicitly remove them after replacing the DB file.

findings.title: Export-failure handler shows 'Restore failed' message
findings.detail: cb_backup_export renders M_BACKUP_RESTORE_FAILED.format(error='غير موجود') (text: 'فشلت الاستعادة' = 'Restore failed') when an export fails. There is no dedicated M_BACKUP_EXPORT_FAILED constant. The test test_cb_backup_export_failure_renders_error actively validates this wrong message.

findings.title: Unused Database import in backups.py
findings.detail: from app.db.database import Database is imported but never referenced (confirmed with pyflakes). The BackupService type is used as a handler parameter, but Database is not.

findings.title: Dead code: ts assigned twice in _make_archive
findings.detail: Line 312 (ts = _now_iso().replace(...)) is immediately overwritten by line 315 (ts = datetime.now(...).strftime(...)). The first assignment is unreachable dead code left from the fix for finding #2.
